report.summary: Reviewed _ollama_native.py: public symbols enumerated, docstring claims checked against code.
risks: effective_input_window | low | Returns max(0, num_ctx - max(0, output_reserve)). If output_reserve > num_ctx, result is 0, which may be surprising but is documented. | Confirm desired behavior with zero input window.

native_chat | medium | force_json parameter typed as object, but docstring says bool or dict; code checks isinstance(force_json, dict) then uses bool(force_json). If force_json is a non-bool non-dict truthy value (e.g. 1), it will set format to 'json', which may be unintended. | Verify callers only pass bool or dict.
_adapt_message | medium | Synthesized tool_call id is 'call_N' which may conflict with real IDs if native endpoint ever provides IDs. | Confirm native endpoint never provides IDs.

_native_messages | medium | The function mutates message dicts by dropping 'id' and 'type' keys, and re-parses arguments from JSON string to dict. If arguments is already a dict, it wraps it in an extra layer? Code: if isinstance(args, str): parse; else keep as is. Then native_calls.append({'function': {'name': ..., 'arguments': args or {}}}). If args is a dict, it's used as-is. That's correct. | No issue.
native_chat | low | num_ctx parameter defaults to None, then uses num_ctx or num_ctx_value(). If num_ctx is 0, it is falsy and falls back to default. | Ensure callers never pass 0.
native_chat | medium | timeout_s parameter defaults to 300, but urllib.request.urlopen may not respect timeout on some platforms. | Test on target OS.

native_chat | low | The docstring says 'format:"json" is sent only when force_json' but code sends format only if force_json is truthy. If force_json is a dict, it sends the dict as the format (schema). That matches docstring. | No issue.

handoff.purpose: Native Ollama /api/chat client with context window control and message adaptation.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_NUM_CTX
symbols.note: Default context window size, measured VRAM-safe for the reference box.

symbols.name: num_ctx_value
symbols.note: Returns the context window to request, from env OLLAMA_NUM_CTX or default, clamped >=2048.

symbols.name: effective_input_window
symbols.note: Returns usable input tokens = context minus output reserve.

symbols.name: _adapt_message
symbols.note: Adapts native /api/chat assistant message to OpenAI shape.

symbols.name: _native_messages
symbols.note: Converts OpenAI-shaped tool_calls back to native form for re-POSTing.

symbols.name: native_chat
symbols.note: POSTs messages to Ollama /api/chat, returns adapted assistant message.

claims.text: Ollama's OpenAI-compat /v1 shim IGNORES a top-level options block (measured this box, 2026-07-26), so it cannot request a larger context window -- an over-budget /v1 request is head-truncated at ~2050 tokens with the 4096 default ctx.
claims.why: Claim about external behavior of Ollama /v1 shim; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: The native /api/chat endpoint honors options.num_ctx, format:"json" and keep_alive -- the three fields the shim silently drops.
claims.why: Claim about Ollama native endpoint behavior; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: DeepSeek is a real external OpenAI API and keeps using _openai_compat; only the local Ollama provider uses this module.
claims.why: Claim about other modules; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: DEFAULT_NUM_CTX = 6144  # Sized by MEASUREMENT on the 15.7GB reference box (2026-07-26), not by the model's 32k max: the runner needs weights (~5GB) PLUS a context-scaled compute/KV buffer, and Ollama OOM-kills the runner when it doesn't fit. num_ctx=16384 -> ~3.9GB buffer: loads on an IDLE box, OOMs mid-session. num_ctx= 8192 -> OOM at 4.3GB free (typical mid-session). num_ctx= 6144 -> loads under the same pressure (~20s cold). Keep this at the measured VRAM-safe value.
claims.why: Claim about measurements and external behavior; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: Env OLLAMA_NUM_CTX overrides the default (see the measured sizing note above; e.g. OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=16384 on an idle box); the value is clamped to >= 2048. An unset or non-integer env value falls back to the default -- this never raises, so a typo in the environment degrades to the safe default instead of crashing an offload.
claims.why: Code checks os.environ.get('OLLAMA_NUM_CTX'), returns DEFAULT_NUM_CTX if None or non-int, and clamps to max(2048, val). No exceptions raised.

claims.text: Usable input tokens = the full requested context minus generation reserve.
claims.why: Code returns max(0, num_ctx_value() - max(0, output_reserve)).

claims.text: Ollama HEAD-truncates an over-long prompt, eating the SYSTEM prompt first.
claims.why: Claim about Ollama server behavior; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: Callers must fail loud against this reserved input budget rather than let the server truncate.
claims.why: Claim about caller behavior; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: Native tool_calls arrive as {"function": {"name", "arguments": <dict>}} with NO id; the OpenAI loop expects arguments to be a JSON STRING and a stable id per call. So we re-serialize arguments with json.dumps and synthesize call_N ids.
claims.why: Code checks if args is not str, then json.dumps it; synthesizes id as f'call_{i}'.

claims.text: The tool_calls key is OMITTED entirely when the native response has none, so callers can do msg.get("tool_calls") or [].
claims.why: Code only adds 'tool_calls' key if native_calls is truthy; otherwise out has no 'tool_calls' key.

claims.text: The agentic loop appends our own _adapt_message output (arguments as a JSON STRING, plus synthesized id/type) back into the history for the next round. Native /api/chat unmarshals arguments into an object and 400s on a string, so here we parse it back to a dict and drop the OpenAI-only id/type keys.
claims.why: Code checks if args is str, then json.loads it; native_calls built without id/type.

claims.text: Messages without tool_calls pass through untouched (same object).
claims.why: Code appends m directly if not calls; no copy, same object reference.

claims.text: options.num_ctx (defaulting to num_ctx_value) is the whole point of this path -- it is the only way to lift the ~2050-token /v1 cap.
claims.why: Claim about /v1 cap; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: num_predict is optional and omitted by default, preserving every existing caller; bounded rewrite callers use it to prevent a malformed JSON generation from consuming the entire remaining context window.
claims.why: Code only adds num_predict to options if num_predict is not None.

claims.text: think is likewise opt-in. Structured edit callers disable hidden reasoning so a bounded generation cannot spend its entire token allowance before emitting the required JSON value.
claims.why: Code only adds think to body if think is not None.

claims.text: format:"json" is sent only when force_json; keep_alive and tools only when provided.
claims.why: Code adds 'format' only if force_json is truthy; adds keep_alive only if not None; adds tools only if truthy.

claims.text: Raises ProviderHTTPError on any HTTP error or an unreachable host, mirroring _openai_compat._post.
claims.why: Code catches HTTPError, URLError, TimeoutError and raises ProviderHTTPError.

claims.text: A dict is a JSON *schema*, and that distinction is load-bearing. format:"json" only promises valid JSON of any shape; a schema constrains the SHAPE at the sampler, masking invalid tokens instead of validating after the fact.
claims.why: Code sets body['format'] = force_json if isinstance(force_json, dict) else 'json'.

observations.what: Module docstring claims about Ollama /v1 shim behavior and measurements; not verifiable from this code.
effective_input_window may return 0 if output_reserve > num_ctx, which is documented but could be unexpected.
force_json parameter typed as object but docstring says bool or dict; code handles both but could accept other truthy values.
_adapt_message synthesizes call ids as 'call_N', which might conflict if native endpoint ever returns ids.
num_ctx parameter defaults to None, then uses num_ctx or num_ctx_value(). If num_ctx is 0 (falsy), falls back to default, which may be unintended.
Timeout handling uses urllib.request.urlopen timeout parameter; may not work on all platforms.
